Rinas

Overview

Rinas is the governor’s court magician on Ingos. A knife associated with him becomes a misleading clue in Brissen’s murder. He admits that a staged caravan was intended to expose raiders and that the nugget had already been stolen. His planned meeting with an informant ends with his own murder; Crooked’s confession identifies the attempt to silence him. [1, 2, 3, 4]

Two magicians on Ingos

Kir and Kel seek magical help on Ingos. Karansul complains about Yam-Akara, whose cheap runes undercut his trade, and identifies Rinas as the governor’s court magician. His receives the travellers with suspicion and later asks them to retrieve materials from his laboratory. Sver the Trapper offers another route: contact Grey Leaf through the Sacred Flower and a vessel from his cache. Grey Leaf explains that the knight Brissen and his magician friend have left for the settlement near the mines. Kir’s first task here is finding an informed ally, before the murder that later dominates the investigation. The vessel Sver asks them to carry is for Woodsfolk balm that eases his own aching joints. He has used their necessary visit to obtain a personal favour. [5, 1, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]

Yam-Akara’s research and the governor’s gift

Yam-Akara introduces himself as a practising magician of the first rank and an honorary member of the Assembly of Magicians of Three Worlds. The elemental samples interest him, and the Joon artifact promises material for a scholarly report. He agrees to search while Kir renews his permit for the mines, where Wormface magic interferes with his measurements. His summons the travellers to Governor Valrasian whether or not his own laboratory errand is complete. The governor demands proper introductions, pays unwelcome attention to Kel and hints at a rare Blue Clan mage’s dart for his collection. Bringing the dart wins the permit, despite his complaints about Yam-Akara’s visits. [11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17]

The planted knife and His’s death

A knife found at the murder site appears to implicate His. The court magician admits it was stolen from his laboratory together with the governor’s nugget. He had sent out the empty caravan to hide that loss and hoped to blame raiders after an informant warned of the planned attack. His arranges a meeting to produce evidence, but is killed before he can clear himself. Meanwhile Geraldine and Karansul disclose their relationship and provide each other with an alibi. Their commercial hostility and private secrecy had made them suspicious without establishing guilt. [18, 2, 3, 19, 20]

Crooked’s confession

The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. His called the same informant to clear his own name; Crooked mistook that invitation for a trap and killed him too. Woodsfolk observations help reconstruct the planted evidence. Before the governor, Kir explains the connected crimes and Crooked admits them. Yam-Akara is released, while the governor reserves Crooked’s punishment for trial. Kel draws the thief out by spreading word that they have found the hidden money. Afterwards the travellers return the recovered communal funds to Geraldine and Trickster. Geraldine wants personal revenge, but Crooked is already in the governor’s custody. [21, 22, 23, 24, 4, 25, 26]
